Looking after yourself while supporting someone with an eating disorder (Easy Read)
It’s important to look after your own physical and mental wellbeing when you’re supporting someone with an eating disorder. Remember you’re not alone and remind yourself the eating disorder is not your fault.
Recognise how challenging it is to support a loved one with an eating disorder. The journey to recovery for your loved one is likely to take some time.
Recovery goes through many stages. You’ll need to adapt to changes to things like care plans and meal plans. This can be difficult for carers and the person with an eating disorder.
If you can, speak to your loved one’s care team for information and advice about eating disorders and looking after yourself.
It’s important to seek help for yourself from organisations like
Beat
and
SupportED
. They can offer support to parents and carers of people with an eating disorder.
Support from friends and family can also be really helpful.
Read more about Beat’s services in Scotland for carers
Support for parents and carers of someone with an eating disorder
Cared Scotland
has information for parents and carers of young people (up to age 25) in Scotland who have recently been diagnosed with an eating disorder and are about to or have just started treatment.
Parent Club
has information and support for parents about eating disorders.
SupportED offer carers in-person and online support including befriending, support groups and training
Feast offers support to families of those affected by eating disorders
YoungMinds offer a
parent helpline and chat service
for information, advice and support.
